hh_keeper.text: Eight hundred years, that tower. I'm only in it forty. But the stairs know me.
When the monks kept it, they burned a fire on the top. It's brighter now. It's also easier on the arms.

hh_greenway.text: I'm doing the Waterford Greenway. Forty-six kilometres, flat the whole way, and a tunnel with the lights on. I've never been happier.
It used to be a railway, and there was no bike in the whole thing. Now there are only bikes. It's a better arrangement.

hh_fisher.text: The Saltees are out there, a few miles. A Wexford man bought one in 1943 and crowned himself prince. Nobody argued. It was cheaper than an argument.
Gannets, puffins, seals. The islands are the best birdwatching in the south-east. And the prince's throne is still out there, a chair on a rock.

champ_hh_lighthouse.text: Ah, you're back. You'll have noticed the lighthouse. It's had a few hundred years' practice at being noticed.

intro: Right so. The light never goes out, and nor do I.
Let me see what the weather's sent me this morning.
champ_hh_lighthouse.win: Fair play. That was as bright as the beam.
champ_hh_lighthouse.tired: Once a week now. Even the light has its off-duty hours. See you Monday.

then.text: The lighthouse has seen worse losses than mine. Probably. Go on, off you go.

else.text: {player}! This lighthouse is one of the oldest working ones in the world. I got the shot, and then a seagull walked into it. Mid-peck. Viral, honestly.
Have you noticed the Irish say 'ah, go on' to mean four different things? I've filmed all four.
Go on, then. A battle, if you fancy it. I'll hold the camera in my teeth.
Fair enough. Save it for when I'm less sweaty.
